description: A four-channel low-frequency oscillator measured in bars rather than hertz: all four share one cycle, each with its own shape and depth, and the bar input locks the whole set to the music

params.text: Sets the rate: locked to a bar it is a division or multiple of the bar, from 64 bars per cycle down to an eighth of a bar; free-running it is 0.02Hz to 20Hz
Fans the four channels apart around the cycle, from all four together at one end of the travel to a full spread at the other
Sets how steady the channels are: at the top of the travel they repeat exactly, and lower down each cycle's depth wanders
Restarts the cycle at the top of the next downbeat on each press
Sets that channel's position around the shape ring — sine, triangle, sawtooth, square, staircase, stepped random and back to sine; with its shape link on it is an offset from the channel above
Sets that channel's depth, from full level clockwise through silence at the centre to full inverted level anticlockwise; with its scale link on it is an offset from the channel above
Links those two channels' shapes, so the lower one follows the upper one with its own knob acting as an offset around the ring
Links those two channels' depths, so the lower one follows the upper one with its own knob acting as an offset

inputs.text: Sets the step grid for the staircase and stepped random shapes: one step per rise, in place of the step count the bar division would give
Sets the timing: the bar length is measured from the time between rises and the cycle is hard-aligned to every downbeat, so it cannot drift however long it runs
A rise restarts the cycle at the top of the next downbeat
Changes the rate or the bar division, added to the frequency knob
Changes the phase spread, added to the phase knob
Changes how far the depth wanders, added to the stability knob
Rotates that channel around the shape ring, added to its shape knob and wrapping rather than stopping at an end
Changes that channel's depth, added to its scale knob

outputs.text: That channel's wave as 0-5V, for levels and cutoffs
That channel's wave as ±5V, the same shape centred on 0V, for pitch, panning and frequency modulation
A trigger each time the cycle comes round to the top

notes: with nothing patched at BAR the module free-runs in hertz like an ordinary low-frequency oscillator; patching BAR hands the timing to the bar and turns the frequency knob into a bar division
all six link buttons come up on, so a fresh module has all four channels ganged to the first; a linked channel's own knob becomes an offset rather than going dead
the stepped random shape draws one fresh set of step voltages per cycle and all four channels share it, so they jump together
